meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Why was Owen's mark changed without anyone calling me?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. And the basis for the zero?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. He could have drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then show me. And did anyone ask Owen about it before the zero went in?
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Students misremember lines. Did you speak to Owen before you entered the zero, yes or no?
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay; that's called revising. I'll want all three of these in writing.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
Fine. You spoke to him. Owen told me he wrote it over the weekend, and a seventeen-year-old put on the spot isn't a transcript.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes under a clock is not the same task as an essay. So what are you proposing, Hale?
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Good, because the company that sells it says it shouldn't stand alone. You still haven't told me what happens to Owen's mark.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
Okay. A private rewrite, not in front of his class, and nothing on his record, in writing tonight. I'll agree to it to put this behind him; everything else goes in my email.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Yes. In writing tonight, copied to the principal.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Thursday, after school. Put the time in the email.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Yes. The apology for how Owen found out goes in that email too.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
The outline, the essay and your November 2 note, attached to that email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday after school, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require the apology for how Owen found out, and the outline, the essay and your November 2 note attached. I expect that confirmation in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Her last position: a private supervised rewrite Thursday after school, the new mark replacing the zero, nothing on his record, confirmed in writing tonight, and she still wants the apology and the three documents attached; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: Your note from November 2, showing you had spoken to Owen before entering the zero, because it answered her question about whether he was heard first.
What cost ground: You let her yes-or-no question about speaking to Owen sit unanswered for several turns, which kept her focused on your process instead of your evidence.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay's writing between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM the night before it was due, which came very close to that night, but it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Put the November 2 conversation with Owen into your opening apology, so she hears that he was heard before the zero without having to ask twice.
